title: The Silent Thief

patient.name: Mr Tan Ah Kow
patient.presenting_complaint: Routine eye check — no specific complaints

history.hpc: Mr Tan presents for a routine eye check at the polyclinic. He denies any eye pain, redness, or sudden vision changes. He mentions his glasses prescription has been stable for years.
history.pmhx: Type 2 diabetes (well-controlled, HbA1c 6.8%), hypertension on amlodipine
history.family_hx: Father had 'eye problems' requiring drops — details unknown
history.social_hx: Non-smoker, occasional alcohol, lives with wife

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Normal cornea, deep anterior chambers, open angles on gonioscopy

fundus.right: C:D ratio 0.7, inferior notching of neuroretinal rim, disc haemorrhage at 6 o'clock
fundus.left: C:D ratio 0.8, superior and inferior notching, peripapillary atrophy

investigations.visual_field: Arcuate scotoma superior field OD, advanced inferior and superior defects OS
investigations.oct_rnfl: Significant thinning inferior and superior quadrants bilaterally

diagnosis: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), moderate OD, advanced OS

immediate: Start prostaglandin analogue — latanoprost 0.005% eye drops, one drop each eye at night
Educate patient on lifelong nature of condition and importance of adherence
Schedule visual field and OCT RNFL in 3 months
follow_up: Target IOP: 30% reduction from baseline (aim <18 mmHg)
If IOP not controlled on monotherapy: add timolol 0.5% BD
Consider selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) if drops insufficient
Refer for trabeculectomy if progressive despite maximum tolerated medical therapy
patient_education: Glaucoma is silent — emphasise no symptoms until late
Compliance with eye drops is critical

key_points: Asks about symptoms (pain, redness, halos, vision loss)
Requests gonioscopy or asks about angle anatomy
Patient education on adherence and family screening
